 Cricket Editorial New Zealand vs India 
 Team management retains faith in Auqib Nabi, he responds with Tim Seifert’s wicket
 India have gone unchanged in the second ODI. Auqib Nabi has made a good start. By Shamik Chakrabarty November 7, 2026 No Comments 2 Mins Read

 India going unchanged in the second ODI in Wellington came as expected. Mohammed Siraj, who joined the squad ahead of this game at Hnry Stadium, was available. But the team management was never going to drop Auqib Nabi after just one outing.
 Nabi conceded 33 runs in six overs without taking a wicket in the series opener in Auckland. But he bowled fairly well, moved the ball both ways and was unlucky not to get Tim Seifert’s wicket early in the game, as Naman Dhir dropped a sitter at square leg. The team management was always going to look beyond the hard numbers. In windy Wellington, with clouds hovering around, conditions appear perfect for him to make a mark. The Jammu and Kashmir seamer has started off by removing Seifert for a duck this time.
 Any suggestion that Siraj has been marginalised would be preposterous. He has joined the squad after playing the four-day tour game for India A against New Zealand A in Lincoln, which ended on Tuesday. He is going to be a vital cog in India’s fast-bowling wheel in the two-Test series against New Zealand that will follow the five ODIs. The Test series starts in Wellington on November 19, and the team management will focus on gradually building his workload for the longer format. Very likely, Siraj will feature in the last two ODIs, which will allow him to get into the rhythm for the Tests, notwithstanding the different format.
 The second ODI was truncated to a 47-over-a-side affair after an hour of play was lost due to rain. At the toss, Shubman Gill, the India captain, told the host broadcaster: “No surprises with the overcast conditions and wicket being under the covers for the last few days. Practice was called off yesterday due to rain but we got good practice in the first game. Haven’t told the boys much, just want to replicate the performance. We are playing the same team.”
 New Zealand, too, were unchanged.
